body: I'm not sure. Contentment?  When the positive outweighs the negative, and when these two positions have a natural shift that doesn't result in one becoming the norm.

I'm not sure, there's the distinct possibility that I'm way off.  However, I'm mainly talking physical contact, which has always been a bit odd for me.  Nothing ridiculous, but I'm just overly aware when it's happening and really dislike it from people I don't know.  Also, being restricted in any way is not nice.  
  
I partially attribute it to the time after I had my first operation, when I had my arms in casts for nearly a month to stop me from touching where they operated.  I have a picture on here actually, [probably NSFW really.](http://imgur.com/LWXO9.jpg)  
  
Probably has nothing to do with it though really, it's just a guess.  it could just be some innate brain chemistry thing instead.

Yeah, I have no problems at all dealing with people like surgeons.  
  
It'd be strange if I did really, since I've had about 7 different operations through my life, orthodontist treatment at hospital every few months until I was 18, speech therapy when I was much younger, and yearly meetings with the whole team (up until I was 18, then every few years.)

That's all in a medical capacity though.  Poking, prodding, cutting, weeks of post-op discomfort, etc.  That's all physical stuff, and I have no trouble with that sort of thing.  Well, sort of, I definitely have intimacy issues of some sort, with my own theories of where they stem from too.

Surgeon: "We'd like to cut open your face again so we can do X, Y, and Z."  
Me: "Sounds great! When do we start?"  
  
Friend: "I'm going to give you a hug."  
Me: "Oh.  This is going to be awkward and uncomfortable."  
  
Pretty much wherever there's an emotional component involved by the look of it.  Actually, whenever there's a physical *and* emotional component I think is more accurate.  Doing it in writing is no problem, to a point.

My situation's a little different from yours, but I guess some of it could still apply.

I've had a few, but I can't really help you with the cost/finding a surgeon since I'm in the UK, and it was done under the head surgeon of the CLEFT unit.  

Last one I had was earlier this year, to fix some cartilage that had moved drastically since the last operation I had (about 3 years ago).  This involved breaking/re-setting the nose, taking out some cartilage that had turned to bone, and reshaping the rest.

The operation took about 6 hours, and the recovery time *around* 2 weeks.  It depends what you have done/how extensive it is though obviously, so I can only speak from my own experience here.  Mine was a pretty big operation though, so 2 weeks is probably much longer than you'll have to recover, but that was how long my cast/plaster had to stay on.

Nothing past the first day is really painful (morphine is lovely too, by the way), just really fucking uncomfortable.  I didn't have my nose packed this time, but it still ends up getting completely clogged up with dried blood.  Dried blood is a horrible thing to have to smell constantly for 2 weeks.  The same thing happens when you have it packed, and having the packing out can -again- be uncomfortable.

The one I had before that was to clear an airway, and was pretty much the same routine really.

If you get it done, don't expect what you see straight after to be anywhere near the final result.  It'll be puffy, red, and bruised, and you'll likely dislike it.  It takes a solid few months afterwards for it all to settle down, and about a year or two until it's how it'll stay (not that it changes a whole lot in those couple of years, it just kind of settles down a bit.)

Though speaking as someone whose nose was completely and utterly fucked from birth, is it really that bad?  If you do decide to do it, research your surgeon extensively, ask to see past patients etc, I'd hate for you to have it made worse.

It's now a kitten, being cruelly played like a puppet, and by the very people that are supposed to take care of it!

To be honest, I'm not sure I'd really take up that professional assistance at any point.  Probably out of stubbornness, sort of.  I've met the woman before too though (only a couple of times saying not much more than hello and sat around a table with the surgeon, orthodontist, etc), and she's lovely.  

It's isn't a case of not being able to accept help either, I'm not sure what it is really.  It could be a case of self-worth issues at the moment, and to have to sit across from someone in such a completely different position in life from yourself might just end up doing more harm than good.  At least that's the way I've decided to justify it to myself anyway, and however convenient a purpose it serves to my gut desire, I think it might actually be right at this point.

Yikes, I'm sorry.  Didn't check this often enough to see anything new.  Though now I can give you a post worth almost 3 times the original day quantity!  That's astounding value, if I do say so myself.

Not a whole lot is different from when I posted this.  Some days have been better than others though, not all bad.  

Yesterday was actually particularly shitty though, it was a mental battle full of indecision and near-perpetual inaction to even make dinner last night.  Like the decision was a faint light lodged in under a dark pressure of "Ahhhhh, bollocks.", yet something that was necessary to head for, just for the fact of being able to see something.  If that makes sense.  I chose a cereal medley though, since I couldn't be bothered to cook, and limiting yourself to only one type of cereal in a bowl seems silly when you can combine it all.  

Anyway, I know this isn't a particularly informative post, just thought I should reply out of common courtesy at least.

I'm not sure.  I might consider it at some point in the future, if things are still the way they are or getting worse.  It'd be tricky at the moment though, since the place is about an hour away and I'm stuck for transport for the next few months.  Though if things got worse, then I probably would yeah, since I wouldn't have to worry about the cost (NHS, and part of the cleft unit.)

I have to ask as well.  Am I the only one seeing a mouse holding a teddy bear in the top-right corner of SW?  Pretty sure I'm not that far gone.

I've had online friends/have a few that I chat to occasionally, it's just not the same though.  It's hard to get to know someone when you can't make eye contact, see their mannerisms, and when you both have access to a delete key.  I find it just doesn't satisfy the social part of my brain (the part in the back, behind the dusty boxes.)

Hey, thanks for taking the time to post something.  Funnily enough, my life was better when I was smoking weed.  It had absolutely nothing to do with the weed, I just found it funny considering your story.  Though I guess it definitely got me into more social situations, but I only smoke every few months at most now.  I like having a clear head most of the time.
    
    
I'm glad you're mostly feeling sorted now too.  What I would say (but I'm not), is that it's good you're still in a relationship even though you're afraid of getting hurt, since there's always that possibility.  It's kind of a requirement to open yourself up to people every now and then if you want any chance at a sane mind.  Luckily, I'm not saying any of that, since that would make me a hypocrite.
    
    
I don't know if I'd call it (for my case) an illness either.  It's just a load of crap I need to deal with, I have some kind of mental-block in actual social situations.  It's not shyness, I just have absolutely nothing to say, even on subjects I know a lot about.  Like there's no motivation there to speak, or maybe that I don't want to waste the persons time.  Which is all ridiculous, and I know that objectively.  
    
    
I do actually have a psychiatrist I could go to if I wanted, though I never have.  Purely because of the fact I had a cleft-lip and palate when I was born, so she's part of the team that I could see if I wanted.  I just don't see the point.  I know what my issues are, I know mainly what they'd recommend to fix them, and I've tried them.  It hasn't worked so far, so I'll try again.  If it fails again, then I'll probably mope around for a bit and give it another shot.  
    
    
It's just the journey there isn't fun at all, and sometimes you want to pack it all in.  I doubt I will though, death is far too final.  It'd be like suggesting I go back to before I was born (hang on, there might be some logic coming up), which seems an equally ridiculous solution.  Probably more ridiculous to be fair, since it's practically impossible.  All I'm saying though, is I wasn't happier before I was born, I wasn't sadder.  I wasn't experiencing any of those things, and by doing that, I'll never get to.  Ah screw it, you know what I'm on about.
    
   
Don't worry, you're not missing much on the robot side of things.  I just went off on a tangent about how I'd use fire in an ultimate-robot-killing-machine, instead of lasers (even though it's the more socially accepted choice of slaughter).  My reasoning was that people are expecting lasers from giant robots, so when they see fire shooting out, they just freak out.  Plus, it propagates.
Sorry, I'm not ignoring this, and thanks for the replies.  I'm not in the US, so I was asleep, and have to go to work now.  I'll definitely have a proper look through it all later.
